body.content:
---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Oeuf Déjeuner <ooeuf.ca@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 29, 2025, 02:29
Subject: Question
To: yan romanowski <romanowskiyan@gmail.com>


Sujets

1). Les échanges pré contrat
*The Exchange Before Signing the Contract*
*At the time these events occurred, we were under pressure due to a
deadline imposed by our landlord to vacate our commercial space. As a
result, we began searching online for a moving company capable of handling
heavy-duty restaurant equipment, as we needed to relocate an entire
pizzeria.*
*During this search, we came across the website of Harmony Movers, a
company located in Lachine, with the destination of the move being LaSalle.
Based on their location and advertised services, we believed this company
to be an appropriate and suitable choice for our needs.*
*We subsequently contacted Harmony Movers by phone and spoke with a company
representative. During this initial conversation, we clearly explained our
situation and specified that the move involved the complete contents of a
pizzeria, including all restaurant equipment. The discussion was explicitly
about moving an entire pizzeria, not a partial or limited selection of
items.*
*During this exchange, the representative requested that we send
photographs of the equipment by text message to the owner of the company,
whose name is Lev. We complied with this request and sent multiple images
via text message. A conversation then took place directly between us and
Lev, during which these images were reviewed.*
*After receiving the images, Lev stated that the move involved only nine
items. However, if one reviews the images that were sent prior to the
signing of the contract, it is clear that this statement does not reflect
the reality shown in the photographs. The images visibly display
significantly more equipment, and by direct observation, approximately 27
separate pieces of equipment can be identified.*
*Furthermore, during these exchanges, we explicitly informed him that the
contract had to include the entire pizzeria equipment. This point was made
clearly and without ambiguity.*
*Following these discussions, Harmony Movers agreed to proceed, provided us
with a price and an estimate, and advised us that in order to reserve the
service, we were required to sign the contract and provide a credit card.
We were informed that the credit card was needed to create and reserve the
contract, and that payment would only be processed once the service was
fully completed and rendered.*
*The contract itself stipulated that the service consisted of transporting
and delivering our equipment to our other location, which was the
agreed-upon destination.*

2) la journée de l’enlèvement au resto ( pas la saisie). Qui y était? À
quelle heure t’es arrivé. Les échanges et discussions . Ce qui n’a pas été
enlevé .
*Events on the Day of the Move*
*On the day of the scheduled move, Pierre Levesque and Costa Cronis were
present on site early in the morning to prepare the premises and ensure
everything was ready for the arrival of Harmony Movers. They arrived on
site at approximately 7:00 a.m. to begin preparations.*
*According to the contract and prior agreement, Harmony Movers was supposed
to arrive at 8:00 a.m., or at the latest 9:00 a.m. However, Harmony Movers
did not arrive within the agreed timeframe. Instead, they arrived at
approximately 11:30 a.m., several hours late.*
*Upon their arrival at 11:30 a.m., the Harmony Movers staff entered the
premises and began walking around, inspecting the equipment and assessing
the scope of the job. For approximately one hour and thirty minutes, no
equipment was moved at all. During this time, the staff did not perform any
moving services and instead stated that they needed to contact their boss
to discuss a different pricing structure, claiming that the job was not
what they thought or what they had agreed to.*
*It was apparent from their conduct that they were attempting to
renegotiate the terms and pricing of the contract after arrival on site. It
also appeared that they were attempting to take advantage of the situation,
given that the owner was of an older age, by pressuring him to agree to a
new arrangement under time constraints.*
*At that point, Pierre Levesque and Costa Cronis discussed the situation
and decided to contact their nephew, Matthew Wallace, to explain what was
happening and seek guidance. After this discussion, Pierre and Costa
stepped away.*
*Despite no work being performed, the Harmony Movers staff remained on site
and continued charging hourly fees, even though they were not moving any
equipment and were only attempting to renegotiate the contract.*
*Pierre Levesque then spoke directly with Matthew Wallace and stated:*
*“Matthew, I do not agree with what they are trying to do right now. We
have a contract, and they are supposed to respect it. We have a deadline.
This equipment must be out of the space by tomorrow. We are not in a
position to call another company. I do not agree with any modification to
this contract.”*
*After this conversation ended, Matthew Wallace contacted Lev, the owner of
Harmony Movers. Matthew explicitly informed Lev that he was on his way to
the site, that he was renting a U-Haul truck in order to move the pastry
equipment into storage, and that he would arrive within approximately one
hour to assess the situation in person.*
*Matthew also made it clear to Lev that:*
*No contract changes were authorized*
*All requests or proposed changes had to be sent by email*
*An explanation was required as to why Harmony Movers was attempting to
change pricing when a contract had already been signed and clearly defined
the scope of work*
*Lev acknowledged this and stated that they would send the information by
email.*
*During this time, Harmony Movers continued attempting to negotiate
directly with Pierre Levesque. Pierre Levesque and Costa Cronis, meanwhile,
continued their duties on site and began preparing the restaurant contents
by placing items into boxes, as the entire restaurant had to be cleared by
the following day.*
*At approximately 2:30 p.m., Matthew Wallace Barnard arrived on site with
two employees. Matthew and his two employees immediately began moving the
pastry equipment into the U-Haul truck parked outside in order to clear
space and comply with the landlord’s deadline.*
*Harmony Movers then began moving some equipment as well. Shortly
thereafter, the owner of Harmony Movers arrived on site. He walked around
the premises inspecting the equipment and approached Matthew Wallace,
asking whether the Coca-Cola refrigerators were for sale, stating that they
might be interested in purchasing them.*
*Matthew replied that all of the equipment belonged to a pizzeria and had
to be relocated to another location, as Pierre Levesque intended to open a
new restaurant elsewhere.*
*The owner then stated that they were not sending an additional truck and
again attempted to push for a change in rates and pricing. Matthew
reiterated that he was not the owner, that he could not authorize any
changes, and that any requests had to be sent by email so the owner could
review them before authorizing anything. This email was not sent
immediately and was only sent later in the afternoon.*
*The job continued for several hours. By approximately 4:00 p.m., Harmony
Movers claimed that their truck was fully loaded and that they needed to
proceed with delivery. Matthew then requested that Harmony Movers assist in
loading some equipment into the U-Haul truck in order to maximize
efficiency and help clear the space, particularly since they were charging
by the hour and were claiming that a second truck would be required.*
*Instead of proceeding to the agreed destination, Harmony Movers left the
site and did not deliver the equipment as stipulated in the contract. They
transported the equipment to their own warehouse and demanded payment
before delivery.*
*Additionally, Harmony Movers left critical equipment behind, including:*
*A double-stack pizza oven*
*Other pizzeria equipment*
*A refrigerator*
*These actions clearly demonstrated that they had no intention of
completing the job as contracted, which required removal and delivery of
all pizzeria equipment to the designated destination.*
*Harmony Movers unilaterally changed the destination, attempted to increase
pricing, and imposed new conditions without any agreement or authorization,
despite the existence of a signed contract that they were obligated to
respect.*
*At this point, Pierre Levesque was in a state of confusion and distress,
but was fully aware that if the equipment was not removed by the next day,
ownership could revert to the landlord. As a result of Harmony Movers’
actions, Pierre Levesque was forced to urgently hire another company to
move the remaining pizza oven, refrigerator, and other equipment that
Harmony Movers had abandoned on site.*

3) les échanges post enlèvement . Les différents montants réclamés
*Unjustified Revised Charges and Attempted Contract Modification*
*Upon reviewing the revised submission that was sent later that same day,
it became clear that Harmony Movers was attempting to impose new and
unjustified charges that were never agreed upon and were not supported by
the facts on site.*
*First, they attempted to charge for a second truck, despite the fact that
no second truck ever arrived on site at any time during the move.*
*Second, they attempted to charge for additional staff. However, the only
additional individuals who arrived on site beyond the original moving crew
were the owners of the company themselves, and these individuals did not
move, lift, or handle any equipment or materials from the premises. No
additional labor services were provided that would justify such charges.*
*Third, they attempted to charge again for heavy-duty or heavyweight
equipment. It is important to note that from the outset, it was clearly
agreed and acknowledged that this was a restaurant move involving heavy
equipment, and a specific fee of $1,800 had already been agreed upon for
heavy-duty equipment and excess weight.*
*Despite this clear agreement, Harmony Movers attempted to charge a second
heavy-equipment fee, amounting to nearly $3,000, effectively billing twice
for the same category of service. This duplication of charges is entirely
inconsistent with the original agreement and has no factual or contractual
basis.*
*These attempted charges are particularly unjustifiable given that Harmony
Movers was fully aware, prior to accepting the job and signing the
contract, that they were coming to move a complete pizzeria, including
restaurant equipment. The nature of the equipment was disclosed, documented
with photographs, and discussed before the contract was executed.*
*The attempt to impose these additional fees, increase the hourly rate, and
introduce a new pricing structure after arrival on site, under severe time
pressure and with full knowledge of the landlord’s eviction deadline, was
not a legitimate contractual adjustment. It constituted an attempt to
coerce payment through pressure, rather than a good-faith modification of
services.*
*At that point, the conduct amounted to extortion, as the company sought to
leverage the urgent circumstances to extract additional payment without
justification, authorization, or contractual support.*
4). La journée de la saisie. Comment ça s’est passé ? Des menaces ? La
police ? Collaboration des employés ? L’avocat a-t-il menacé ou tenter
d’intimider le huissier ? Quels équipements manquent ? Ça va pendre un
estimé des réparations et valeur de l’équipement manquants
*Harmony Movers, The Story (Continued)*

*Missing Equipment and Final Documentation*

*After completing a full inspection of the storage areas and the 53-foot
container, it became evident that a significant amount of equipment was
missing.*

*Using the affidavits and inventory lists, the bailiff carefully:*

*Verified which equipment had been recovered*

*Identified which items were not present*

*Formally noted all missing equipment*


*All related documents were then handed over to the representative of
Harmony Movers, and we were authorized to leave the premises.*


*---*

*Delivery to the Original Contract Destination*

*Once the recovery process was completed, all retrieved equipment was
transported to 5505 Rue Irwin, LaSalle, Québec, which was:*

*The original destination*

*Clearly stated in the initial contract*

*Where the equipment should have been delivered in the first place by
Harmony Movers*


*This additional handling was required solely because Harmony Movers failed
to complete their contractual obligations.*


*---*

*Obstruction, Stalling, and Intimidation*

*Throughout the process, we spent an excessive amount of time searching for
goods that were not located where Harmony Movers claimed they were stored.*

*The landlord:*

*Refused to assist*

*Actively stalled operations*

*Appeared to be waiting for his lawyer in an attempt to override or delay
enforcement of the bailiff’s order*


*He:*

*Instructed employees not to identify themselves*

*Directed staff to call the police*

*Attempted to intimidate and delay the lawful recovery of goods*



*---*

*Condition of the Equipment*

*Upon inspection, we found equipment:*

*Lying directly on the floor*

*With broken doors*

*With compressors hanging*

*Stored in a disorganized, unsafe, and negligent manner*


*This condition was entirely inconsistent with the state of the equipment
at the time it was picked up from: 6241 Boulevard Léger, Montréal-Nord, H1J
6K4.*


*---*

*Request for Video and Photo Evidence*

*Harmony Movers has stated that:*

*They possess video footage*

*They documented the pickup and handling of the equipment*


*We are formally requesting that:*

*All videos*

*All photographs*

*All documentation related to the pickup, transport, handling, and storage*


*be submitted to the court, in order to demonstrate:*

*How the equipment was moved*

*How it was stored*

*The condition in which it was maintained*


*Given that Harmony Movers advertises itself as a leading company in
Montréal for heavy equipment handling, the level of negligence observed is
inexplicable and unacceptable.*


*---*

*Contractual Breaches and Billing Irregularities*

*Under the original contract, Harmony Movers agreed to:*

*Arrive at 8:00 a.m. (9:00 a.m. at latest)*

*Pick up all equipment*

*Deliver everything directly to 5505 Rue Irwin, LaSalle*


*Harmony Movers later claimed there were only 9 photos documenting the
pickup.*
*However:*

*Images sent to Lev’s phone clearly total 17 photos*

*These images show approximately 27 separate pieces of equipment*


*This discrepancy raises serious concerns regarding misrepresentation and
billing manipulation.*


*---*

*Unauthorized Charges and Revised Billing*

*Harmony Movers later attempted to:*

*Add hourly charges for an extra worker (never provided)*

*Charge for a second truck (never used)*

*Add charges for “unexpected heavy equipment”*


*However:*

*A prior agreed charge of $1,800 for heavy equipment already existed in the
signed contract*

*This charge was accepted by both parties*

*No additional heavy-equipment fees were justified*


*These revised charges were not authorized and did not reflect services
actually rendered.*


*---*

*Intentional Contract Violation*

*Harmony Movers attempted to:*

*Replace the original contract with new rules and conditions*

*Demand compliance with their revised billing and procedures*


*Quadro Holding Ltée expressly refused, stating that:*

*Only the original signed contract applied*

*Any deviation constituted a breach*


*The contract:*

*Was signed by Pierre Lévesque*

*Included a credit card on file*

*Clearly stated that payment is due once the service is fully completed*



*---*

*Failure to Complete Service*

*Harmony Movers:*

*Left equipment behind at 6241 Boulevard Léger*

*Failed to deliver all goods to 5505 Rue Irwin*

*Redirected equipment to their storage facility without authorization*


*They then:*

*Refused to deliver the remaining equipment*

*Demanded payment for revised charges*

*Forced Quadro Holding to:*

*Find another moving company*

*Obtain additional insurance*

*Assume risks that were not part of the original agreement*




*---*

*Refusal of Credit Card Payment*

*Despite the contract clearly stating that:*

*Credit card payment was mandatory*

*The card would be charged upon completion of service*


*Harmony Movers:*

*Refused credit card payment*

*Demanded cash or certified cheque*

*Prevented the client from contesting charges*


*This refusal appears intentional, particularly in light of:*

*Missing equipment*

*Damaged goods*

*Incomplete service*



*---*

*Conclusion*

*Quadro Holding Ltée:*

*Refused to sign any revised agreements*

*Refused unauthorized billing*

*Acted strictly in accordance with the original contract*


*The condition of the equipment, the missing items, and the refusal to
complete delivery fully justify Quadro Holding’s position.*

*Harmony Movers:*

*Failed to respect the contract*

*Withheld goods*

*Imposed unauthorized charges*

*Neglected equipment*

*Obstructed lawful recovery*

*Attempted to force payment before service completion*

*Harmony Movers, The Story*

*Chronology of Events – Thursday*

*On Thursday morning, I presented myself at 9:00 a.m. at the premises of
Harmony Movers for the recovery of restaurant equipment that had been
seized and retained by Harmony Movers following a delivery in June.*

*To execute this recovery properly, I had:*

*Hired five employees*

*Secured one truck*

*Reserved a storage unit*


*All arrangements were made to efficiently retrieve the equipment under
legal authority.*


*---*

*Arrival and Initial Refusal*

*At approximately 10:00 a.m., a huissier (bailiff / justice officer)
arrived on site.*
*We entered the reception area and were greeted by a secretary.*

*We clearly informed her that:*

*We were there to retrieve seized goods*

*We had proper judicial documentation*

*The huissier was present to execute a court order*


*The secretary immediately refused access, stating she needed to contact
her boss.*

*After calling him, she informed us that the owner of Harmony Movers
refused to release any goods unless a balance of $4,500 was paid.*

*The bailiff explicitly stated that:*

*He was not there to negotiate*

*His role was to execute the judge’s order*

*Payment disputes were not relevant to the enforcement of the court
decision*



*---*

*Obstruction and Intimidation*

*The bailiff asked the secretary to identify herself.*
*She refused to do so and stated that police would be called to evict us if
we did not leave.*

*The bailiff then:*

*Presented his official identification and badge*

*Explained clearly that she did not have the authority to refuse compliance*


*A manager or director then intervened, attempting to diffuse the
situation. She stated that:*

*There were “no bosses available”*

*They were not authorized to allow entry or release of goods*


*At this point, the bailiff stated he would:*

*Return to the Palais de Justice de Montréal*

*Obtain additional enforcement authorization*

*Secure authority to enter the premises, change locks if required, and
recover the goods with police assistance*


*He then left.*


*---*

*False Cooperation and Continued Refusal*

*Approximately 10 minutes later, the same lady exited the building and told
me:*

*They were not refusing access*

*They needed to send documentation to the owner to obtain authorization*


*I immediately contacted the huissier, asking him to return.*

*Upon his return, the staff demanded that:*

*He photograph their internal documents*

*Without granting access to the premises*


*The bailiff refused, explaining that:*

*He does not photograph internal company documents*

*Copies would be formally provided after his report was completed*


*Once again, access was refused, and the landlord stated he would call the
police.*

*To avoid further delay, the bailiff left again to obtain stronger court
enforcement authority.*


*---*

*Police Intervention and Forced Access*

*After approximately three hours, the bailiff returned, this time
accompanied by police officers.*

*Due to:*

*Persistent refusal*

*Obstruction*

*Intimidation*

*Threats involving police*


*The authorities informed Harmony Movers that:*

*Failure to comply would result in arrests*


*At that point, the staff stated they wanted no involvement and told police
and the bailiff to do whatever was necessary.*
